policy: A reading a second pass found wrong is not published as the answer. It is published as part of the case: this word names somebody, here is the record the review named, here is what was ruled out and on what evidence. Where the review named a referent no dataset holds, the record is written here and says who else it might be.

The land the eagle carries Jehoiachin to, which the verse calls a land of traders; the encyclopedia holds it, and the candidate list for this Hebrew name did not offer it.

create.distinguisher: who stood at Ezra's right hand as he read the Law (NEH 8:4)
create.notes: A contemporary of Ezra, not the pre-exilic Hilkiah son of Shallum in Ezra's own genealogy. The encyclopedia's record merges the two, which is why its distinguisher names this verse while its own verse list does not.

alternatives.reason: The record the reading chose, and the one the encyclopedia's own verse list gives this verse to. The audit of 2026-09-06 by claude-opus-5 under prompt audit-1 ruled it out at high confidence: A contemporary of Ezra, not Ezra's pre-exilic great-grandfather; the record wrongly merges the two. Nobody has shown that the two are not one man; what has been shown is that the record does not fit the verse.

The adjudication of 2026-09-06, judged by claude-opus-5 with the evidence rebuilt from the corpus and every case escalated to claude-fable-5-1 overturned it and named shebaniah-2: BibleData partitions the four Shebaniahs of Nehemiah 10 cleanly — the priest at 10:4, shebaniah-4 at 10:10, shebaniah-2 at 10:12 — and the parenthetical *(v10 and v12)* in shebaniah-4's distinguisher reads more naturally as *the two Levite Shebaniahs are at v10 and v12, and this is the other one* than as a claim to both. The model's reading puts two records on one word. What the text does not settle is which of the two sealers is the Levite of Nehemiah 9:4, and BibleData's answer to that is a convention rather than a demonstration.
